newsitem.title: GERMANY: Deutsche Telekom is 66 billion mark company.
newsitem.headline: Deutsche Telekom is 66 billion mark company.

text.p: Deutsche Telekom, the German phone monopoly, will become a publicly traded company on November 18 after its huge public offering: Here is a snapshot:
CAPITAL STOCK: 2 billion shares, nominal value of 5 marks per share.
IPO: Up to 713 million shares at 28.50 marks.
MANAGEMENT BOARD: CEO Ron Sommer, CFO Joachim Kroeske, Detlev Buchal, Hagen Hultzsch, Heinz Klinkhammer, Herbert May, Erik Jan Nederkorn, Gerd Tenzer.

AREAS OF BUSINESS: Fixed-network and mobile telephone services for business and private customers; leased line, data transmission, text, online and networking services; cable television and broadcasting stations.
SUBSIDIARIES: Deutsche Telekom MobilNet GMBH; Online Pro Dienste GmbH.

INTERNATIONAL VENTURES: Atlas partnership with France Telecom. Global One joint venture with France Telecom and Sprint. Controlling stake in Hungary's Matav. Minority stakes in Philippine, Indonesian and Malaysian phone ventures. Stakes in mobile phone companies in Russia and Belarus.

MAIN COMPETITORS: Mannesmann, which has a competing mobile phone service and is building an alternative fixed network using German railway's DBKom network. Mannesmann, AT&T Corp and Unisource NV will take a stake in DBKom.
Vebacom, a venture linking electric utility Veba and Britain's Cable & Wireless, and new partner, utility RWE. VIAG, another utility that has teamed up with British Telecom.

REGULATION: The German Telecommunications Act on August 1 opened to competition all services except voice service over public phone lines. The European Union deregulates all telecoms markets Jan 1, 1998.
HISTORY: Originated as part of German postal authority. Separated from postal service in 1989. Became stock corporation Jan 1, 1995. -- Bonn Newsroom, 49 228 26097150
